races.name: ZYN In The Moment British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
John Banks Group Front Runner Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Love Me Bae
runners_data.note: Holds up in races but carries a significant fade-in-finish flag that is particularly damaging in a slowly run three-runner race; Pat Cosgrave partners her for Adam Kirby's yard (1/12 in the last 14 days) and she arrives 18 days since her last run having finished ninth and off the board in her two starts, both on soft ground, which is a surface step up here on Good to Firm.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden's filly (7/25 in 14 days) arrives off a creditable second on soft ground at 7f, stepping up in trip for the first time; Robert Havlin takes the ride and the yard's strong recent form is the primary angle, with the hold-up style perfectly suited to a slow-run sprint finish on this track.

runners_data.name: Yimmna
runners_data.note: William Haggas saddles this lightly raced filly (10/27 in 14 days) who is unknown in terms of tactical positioning; she ran seventh on her sole start over 7f on soft ground at Sandown, making the trip and going step-up here genuine unknowns, and Tom Marquand will need to coax an improved display from a filly whose profile remains largely unreadable.

races.paceDynamic: All three fillies are mapped as hold-up or unknown style runners, meaning none of Love Me Bae, Starlight Lass, or Yimmna is likely to assert early and set a genuine tempo. With no natural front-runner in a three-runner field over a flat Newmarket mile on Good to Firm ground, the race will almost certainly crawl through the early and middle stages before quickening sharply into the Dip. Love Me Bae carries a notable fade-in-finish flag that becomes particularly damaging in a slow-run race that turns into a sprint, while Yimmna's lightly raced profile means her finishing resolution is unproven under pressure. This race shape — a tactical, slowly run contest resolved by a punchy late burst — favours the runner with the cleanest, most reliable finishing kick, and on that basis Starlight Lass's Gosden credentials and two-runner form make her the natural beneficiary of a compression finish.

scenarios.title: Slow Crawl Sprint Finish

scenarios.body: If the field drifts at a crawl and the race is decided by a sharp final-furlong burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Takes Command Early
scenarios.trigger: If Yimmna or Love Me Bae elects to race more prominently than mapped and seizes a front position.
scenarios.body: If Yimmna or Love Me Bae elects to race more prominently than mapped and seizes a front position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up early and the race becomes a true test of stamina over the mile trip.
scenarios.body: If the pace picks up early and the race becomes a true test of stamina over the mile trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse makes the running but fades badly in the final furlong, gifting the race to those closing.
scenarios.body: If a horse makes the running but fades badly in the final furlong, gifting the race to those closing.

watchPoints.text: Love Me Bae has a flagged fade-in-finish tendency — watch whether Pat Cosgrave attempts to ride her more prominently to counteract this, as her hold-up style in a three-runner tactical race leaves her badly exposed if the sprint develops too sharply.

Yimmna is lightly raced and her style is genuinely unknown — watch the early stages to see whether Tom Marquand allows her to drift back into last or attempts to press forward, as that decision will define her chance in a field this small.

With no confirmed pace-setter, watch the opening two furlongs closely — if all three fillies settle conservatively, the effective race distance shrinks to a 2f dash and finishing-kick quality becomes the only differentiator.

Starlight Lass steps up from 7f to 1m for the first time — watch how Robert Havlin positions her through the middle stages, as a horse who gets outpaced if the sprint fires too early could be caught flat-footed despite the Gosden formbook behind her.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race per the going report — watch for any filly who appears to be travelling less fluently than expected in the middle mile, as all three have softer-ground form, and the faster surface introduces a small unknown for each runner.

races.name: ZYN Pacesetter Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Angel Shared
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Steph Hollinshead who needs traffic to part; her similar-going record of 3W5P over 5-6f on Good is encouragingly solid, though her last four runs show no better than fifth and this flat 6f on Good to Firm asks her to find more than she has recently shown.|

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly carries a pelham (hg:p) and has placed twice in her last three over this 6f trip on Good — she is actually a hold-up horse by nature, tucked to midfield here only because the rear is congested with similar types, so her true finishing kick arrives later than her map position implies.|

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Jonathan Portman, uncontested and likely to set her own fractions; her two recent seconds over 6-7f on Good and Soft demonstrate consistency, and with a 45-day break she arrives fresh, though the step back to 6f from 7f is a slight question on whether she gets home or gets caught.|

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: A six-year-old who has shown honest placed form over 6f on Good for Michael Herrington, but her natural running style sits further back than her midfield slot here — she is a true hold-up type repositioned forward on the map purely due to the volume of closers in this field, and without a strong pace to run into, her chance is structurally compromised.|

runners_data.name: Eskimo Pie
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides this Jane Chapple-Hyam three-year-old who has placed three times in five recent runs but never won; her form is over 7-8f more often than 6f and the step down in trip on Good to Firm is a query, though she is the type to pick up late if gaps appear.|

runners_data.name: Lara Antipova
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's lightly raced three-year-old has an excellent form profile — two wins and a second from three starts, all over 6f on Standard or Good — and Charles Bishop can position her ideally just off the pace with only 73 days between runs presenting the only mild flag; this is the most progressive profile in the field.|

runners_data.name: There's A Chance
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's filly has won twice over 6f including on Good ground and Neil Callan knows how to place a prominent racer on a flat straight track; her trainer's T14 strike rate of 5/35 is modest but the horse's own form (1-3-7-8-1) shows she shows up when conditions suit and this shape fits her well.|

runners_data.name: Polka Blue
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this Charles Hills three-year-old who has won back-to-back on Standard and Good; she is a natural front-runner by inclination but the presence of Brisk Symphony as the confirmed leader means she is very unlikely to get her favoured forward berth, and racing restrained against her instincts on Good to Firm tempers her appeal despite the progressive form string.|

races.paceDynamic: Brisk Symphony is the confirmed sole front-runner here and, with no credible challenger for the lead, Rob Hornby can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this Good to Firm 6f at Newmarket's July course. Lara Antipova and There's A Chance are genuine prominent types who will press forward behind her, creating a two-or-three wide bracket just off the pace, while Polka Blue — though a natural prominent racer — is likely to be squeezed back from her preferred position given the traffic in the first two furlongs. The field holds more prominent types than the shape can comfortably accommodate at the front: Polka Blue, Shallow, and Powdering are all racing out of their natural positions, with Lara Antipova and There's A Chance best placed to secure the ground just off the leader. This race shape — a lone front-runner dictating a fair but uncontested tempo with a small group pressing — heavily favours horses who can race prominently in the slipstream and produce a sustained finish, rather than genuine closers who will struggle for clear daylight in a small, compressed field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brisk Symphony Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Brisk Symphony secures an uncontested lead and the gallop is fair but never frantic, allowing her to conserve enough energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: If Brisk Symphony secures an uncontested lead and the gallop is fair but never frantic, allowing her to conserve enough energy to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lara Antipova or There's A Chance settle just off the pace and produce the superior finishing kick in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Lara Antipova or There's A Chance settle just off the pace and produce the superior finishing kick in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flyer Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to create a gap and one of the deeper closers, Angel Shared or Eskimo Pie, finds a clear run to pick up late.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough to create a gap and one of the deeper closers, Angel Shared or Eskimo Pie, finds a clear run to pick up late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Redistributed Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo accelerates sharply mid-race, burns out Brisk Symphony, and the true hold-up types Shallow and Powdering find room to close.
scenarios.body: If the tempo accelerates sharply mid-race, burns out Brisk Symphony, and the true hold-up types Shallow and Powdering find room to close.

watchPoints.text: Lara Antipova is lightly raced and rapidly progressive — if Charles Bishop slots her directly behind Brisk Symphony in the first two furlongs, she has the most upwardly mobile profile in the field and could prove the biggest danger to the front-runner inside the final furlong.

Polka Blue's style conflict is a material risk to her chance — watch whether Tom Marquand pushes forward to contest the lead early, as any energy burned fighting Brisk Symphony for position on Good to Firm could blunt her finish significantly.

There's A Chance finished eighth last time on Good over 6f but won on the same surface over the same trip previously — her form figures need reading carefully as the wide draw or pace scenario may have been the issue, not the conditions.

The going report consistently shows Good to Firm for this 6f slot across all races, despite the race card listing Good — confirm the actual strip underfoot, as any genuine softening would shift the balance toward horses with Soft form like Angel Shared and away from the prominent types.

Brisk Symphony's 45-day absence is the key watch point if she is race-rusty in the early strides — any hesitation at the break or failure to stride on immediately will allow Lara Antipova or There's A Chance to take her position and fundamentally alter the race shape.

races.name: Air Charter Service Handicap

runners_data.name: Phantom Watch
runners_data.note: Best recent form in the race with a win at 8f on Good and three places on similar going; Billy Loughnane is a natural fit at this venue and Hugo Palmer's 4/46 14-day record is modest but the horse's own profile makes it the most interesting hold-up type here — visor worn adds a small concern but form is compelling.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Zero wins from six sim-going runs and a string of single-digit finishes; a true hold-up operator who has been placed in midfield on the map but will want to race even further back, which in a field running at a controlled pace severely limits its chance.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter with a 1W6P record in sim-going and recent thirds in good company; naturally wants to come from the rear but with so many hold-up horses jostling for the same ground, its legitimate closing run may be blocked — the STYLE_FIT tag is earned but its form merits respect if it finds daylight.

runners_data.name: Poke The Bear
runners_data.note: Zero wins from fifteen sim-going runs and a 0-4 trainer record in the last 14 days; genuinely wants to close from the back but the going-concern flag (turf-only) on what is Good to Firm combined with a poor recent sequence including a seventh make this difficult to fancy even if it gets its preferred position.

runners_data.name: Khuskhas
runners_data.note: Placed in blinkers (first-time headgear flag) and with a 42-day absence, James Ferguson's runner brings some freshness but its sim-going record is sparse; naturally a hold-up type pushed into the midfield mix, its best form came over shorter and the step to a straight mile on quick ground is not obviously ideal.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: 71 days off the track is significant for a lightly-raced three-year-old, and its best form (a second over 8f on standard) came when it got a clear run from a genuine hold-up position; Charlie Clover's 1/5 14-day record is fine but the layoff and redistribution from true back-of-field position makes it hard to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Hour By Hour
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose recent form reads 7-8-8-0-0 with all last five runs on standard or soft/heavy going; the switch to Good to Firm is a meaningful concern and Adam Kirby training is a relatively new venture — this profile does not scream competitiveness at this trip and going combination.

runners_data.name: Double Time
runners_data.note: 160-day absence is the defining angle here; won over 8f on standard going and has the weight to carry (141lbs), and Tim Vaughan's 0/8 14-day record offers no stable confidence — the gelding needs the run to strip fitter and its best chance relies on a chaotic race which is the least likely scenario.

runners_data.name: Just Typical
runners_data.note: The sole front runner in the race and therefore holds the critical positional advantage; Ryan Kavanagh's 5lb claim keeps weight manageable and Ian Williams' 1/27 14-day strike rate is poor, but this horse's entire chance rests on the pace dynamic rather than stable form — controlling from the front on Good to Firm over a straight mile is a genuinely powerful weapon in this field composition.

races.paceDynamic: Just Typical is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will stride into an uncontested position from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight mile. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Daretobedifferent, Norcross Brow, Khuskhas, Big Alex Walmsley and Poke The Bear are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map positions because there are simply too many closers and not enough natural prominent racers to fill those slots; Just Typical and possibly Hour By Hour are the only runners likely to genuinely press forward. With one horse controlling a measured pace and the closers bunched behind unable to all get a clean run in a compressed field, the race shape overwhelmingly favours the front runner to dictate and any horse comfortable tracking in second or third who can quicken when the pace is honest but not punishing. Hold-up horses face a compounded disadvantage: not only must they overcome a steady gallop from off the pace, but several are not true hold-up types and will likely find themselves stuck in traffic rather than in the clear ground at the rear they need.

scenarios.title: Just Typical Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Just Typical leads at a honest but uncontested pace and the closers cannot reel in a horse with a significant lead advantage on Good to Firm.
scenarios.body: If Just Typical leads at a honest but uncontested pace and the closers cannot reel in a horse with a significant lead advantage on Good to Firm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracking Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Just Typical sets a genuinely strong pace that leaves it vulnerable in the final furlong and a close-tracking type delivers a well-timed challenge.
scenarios.body: If Just Typical sets a genuinely strong pace that leaves it vulnerable in the final furlong and a close-tracking type delivers a well-timed challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Running
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the entire field closes in a fast-finishing heap.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the entire field closes in a fast-finishing heap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow early, the field concertinas and the race becomes a sprint finish with no meaningful positional advantage.
scenarios.body: If the pace is too slow early, the field concertinas and the race becomes a sprint finish with no meaningful positional advantage.

watchPoints.text: Just Typical is the only confirmed pace setter in a field of nine and if Ryan Kavanagh (5lb claimer) judges the fractions well, the horse could prove very difficult to catch — watch for whether anyone challenges for the lead in the first furlong because if no one does, Just Typical's advantage compounds every stride.

Phantom Watch is the form pick and Billy Loughnane will need to slot in second or third to maximise its closing kick — watch for where it settles in the first two furlongs; if it gets trapped in a wall of hold-up horses it loses its ability to track and pounce.

The redistribution of Daretobedifferent, Norcross Brow, Khuskhas, Big Alex Walmsley and Poke The Bear into midfield slots means there is a real risk of traffic congestion between the two-furlong and one-furlong poles — watch for a bunching episode that benefits Just Typical at the expense of multiple closers simultaneously.

Double Time's 160-day absence combined with 141lbs and a trainer without a recent winner is a combination to note — if this horse shows significant early drift in the market it confirms the stable is not confident it is race-fit.

Hour By Hour's last five runs all came on standard or soft going and the switch to Good to Firm at Newmarket is a surface concern worth monitoring in the paddock for any signs of scratchy movement before the race.

races.name: debenhams.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Maith Mar Or
runners_data.note: Unclassified style for John Berry's 3yo who has been absent 218 days; the lone form win came over a similar trip on standard ground, but finishing positions of 3-5-4 tell a modest story and a return from seven months off at this level demands significant market support to trust.

runners_data.name: Jodhpur Blue
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' 5yo has strong staying credentials on the all-weather (five of last five runs on Tapeta/Polytrack) and while his natural instinct is to race from the rear of the field, the race map has him shown in midfield only because there are more hold-up types here than the chart can accommodate behind them; on fast Newmarket turf and over 1m2f he has questions to answer for fitness after 98 days off.

runners_data.name: Rockafeller Skank
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's 3yo arrives in the best form of the field — four consecutive wins including on good and soft ground — and George Wood takes over the reins on a horse that has shown it can quicken sharply; a natural hold-up runner whose profile screams sprint-finish beneficiary, the 8-day turnaround is not a concern for a horse clearly in the form of its life.

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand is a high-quality booking for S Woods' 3yo who wears a hood and was placed last time from a hold-up position; similar-going form shows no wins from five attempts but the trip looks a natural fit, and Marquand's ability to find a position from the back in a slowly-run race is arguably the most important factor in how this horse performs.

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up or unconfirmed style and no genuine front-runner in the field, this 1m2f contest at Newmarket's July course is almost certain to crawl early before erupting into a sprint finish from the Dip. Jodhpur Blue, Rockafeller Skank, and Booziebrunch are all natural hold-up types who will be content to track a pace that nobody wants to set, meaning the tempo is likely to be genuinely slow through the first half of the race. Maith Mar Or's unclassified style adds no certainty — if anything, one of the more forward-thinking jockeys may be forced to take up a reluctant lead simply to avoid racing in a dawdle. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can usefully separate, and Jodhpur Blue — a true rear-of-field operator — has been mapped to midfield purely as an artefact of that congestion; the race shape strongly favours those with a sharp, late turn of foot who can quicken quickly on fast ground rather than grinders who need a true end-to-end gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bunched Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race degenerates into a six-furlong dash from the two-pole, the fastest accelerator wins.
scenarios.body: If the field crawls early and the race degenerates into a six-furlong dash from the two-pole, the fastest accelerator wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow-Burn Grind
scenarios.trigger: If one runner — most likely by default rather than design — drifts to the front and sets a modest but steady tempo that stretches the field slightly.
scenarios.body: If one runner — most likely by default rather than design — drifts to the front and sets a modest but steady tempo that stretches the field slightly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Maith Mar Or Leads
scenarios.trigger: If Alexandra Egan elects to send Maith Mar Or forward from the wide draw to try to control the race and set a manageable pace from the front.
scenarios.body: If Alexandra Egan elects to send Maith Mar Or forward from the wide draw to try to control the race and set a manageable pace from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Outpaced
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so muddling and stop-start that horses unable to quicken sharply from off it — including Jodhpur Blue, whose hold-up style is compromised by the congested field — get outsprinted by a sharp-actioned rival.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is so muddling and stop-start that horses unable to quicken sharply from off it — including Jodhpur Blue, whose hold-up style is compromised by the congested field — get outsprinted by a sharp-actioned rival.

watchPoints.text: Rockafeller Skank carries the most live form in the race — four wins on the bounce — and if this turns into the anticipated sprint finish its sharp acceleration on good-to-firm ground could make it very hard to beat.

Jodhpur Blue's true running style is hold-up on the all-weather; racing on fast turf for the first time in its recent history and coming back after 98 days, the style mismatch and fitness query both need monitoring in the market.

With no confirmed front-runner, watch whether Maith Mar Or's jockey Alexandra Egan (claiming 7lb) is instructed to take up the lead by default — if so, the race shape changes materially and the pace probe above is invalidated.

Booziebrunch is fitted with a hood and Tom Marquand rides; headgear plus a top jockey on a horse with placed form over course and distance suggests the trainer believes there is more to come, and a significant market move should be treated as significant information.

The going report consistently lists this race as Good To Firm despite the racecard showing Good — all runners are marked going:OK but the actual surface is faster than billed, which may particularly favour Rockafeller Skank whose best form has come on quicker ground.

races.name: Boodles Handicap

runners_data.name: Amorim
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for George Boughey with Billy Loughnane aboard; has placed twice at 6f on Good ground but this 7f trip is a step up in distance with no win at the trip — the extra furlong is an open question, and he arrives 25 days fresh with a tongue-tie fitted.

runners_data.name: Marengo Storm
runners_data.note: Finley Marsh takes the ride for Richard Hughes; natural front-running speed is the asset here but three runs have all been over 6f, meaning today's 7f trip is unexplored territory — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that his prominent role is genuine but converting it over the extra furlong on this flat course is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old arrives with the strongest 7f credentials in the field, carrying a 2W4P record in similar going and back-to-back placed efforts over today's trip on Good ground; Tom Marquand's patient riding style suits tracking Marengo Storm before delivering a challenge, and 48 days since last run is the only mild caution.

races.paceDynamic: Marengo Storm is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner field and will go forward to lead from the outset, setting what projects to be a controlled, uncontested gallop over 7f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket. With no rival willing or likely to challenge for the lead, the pace will be honest but not pressured, creating a steady-to-fair tempo rather than a true test of stamina. Hardy's Hero and Amorim will both be tracking from prominent-to-hold-up positions, with Hardy's Hero likely closer to the pace given his prominent style and strong form at 7f. This race shape — a single unchallenged leader on a flat, fast track — classically favours a prominent chaser with a proven finishing kick at the trip, and Hardy's Hero's course-and-distance profile makes him the prime beneficiary of this setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Late Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Marengo Storm controls a measured gallop and the two chasers close in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Marengo Storm controls a measured gallop and the two chasers close in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Marengo Storm builds a decisive lead and the hold-up horses fail to close on the flat Newmarket straight.
scenarios.body: If Marengo Storm builds a decisive lead and the hold-up horses fail to close on the flat Newmarket straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is quick enough to expose Marengo Storm and Amorim produces a strong late run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is quick enough to expose Marengo Storm and Amorim produces a strong late run from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: All Three Tight Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that all three runners enter the final furlong in a heap with little to choose between them.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so moderate that all three runners enter the final furlong in a heap with little to choose between them.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hardy's Hero tracks Marengo Storm closely from the outset — if Marquand times his move off the final bend, Hardy's Hero's proven 7f form on this going makes him the chief threat to the leader.

Marengo Storm's uncontested lead is the race's defining factor, but the jump from 6f to 7f is unproven; monitor if Finley Marsh sets a genuinely sustainable pace or if the extra furlong finds him out in the final 100 yards.
Amorim's tongue-tie is new headgear worth noting — if it has a sharpening effect and Loughnane presses forward, the three-runner dynamic could change significantly from what the pace map suggests.
With only three runners on Good to Firm ground, the draw and early positioning will be magnified — any stumble or slow break from any runner could reshape the entire tactical picture instantly.

races.name: Dereham Handicap

runners_data.name: Vilaine Verlaine
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's 4yo has run twice at 16f including a recent second at Stratford, and the step back to Good To Firm turf at Newmarket is a fair test; her modest trainer 14-day strike rate (1/10) offers little confidence, but she holds a legitimate each-way claim if the slow-pace sprint finish develops cleanly from the rear.

runners_data.name: Now The Eagle
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's 4yo is the form pick in this contest, with a win and two seconds from three starts over 16f at Stratford showing genuine aptitude for the trip; 25 days since last run is manageable, and Ryan Kavanagh's 5lb claim could sharpen the response in a sprint finish — the key question is whether Good To Firm Newmarket suits as well as soft-biased Stratford.

runners_data.name: Prince Quattro
runners_data.note: James Owen's 7yo has a reasonable placed record at this distance on artificial surfaces, but the 92-day layoff is a significant concern, and his natural running style means he will be operating ahead of where he would ideally race — the STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine deterrent to rating him highly in a shape that does not accommodate his true finishing instincts.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse
runners_data.note: S Woods's 4yo returns just 8 days after its last start wearing a hood, and while two places from five runs at 14-16f shows consistency, the going report confirms Good To Firm throughout the card — Billy Loughnane has the experience to adapt tactically, but this horse's optimal profile is not served by being shuffled forward out of its natural hold-up role.

runners_data.name: Dereham
runners_data.note: John Berry's veteran 10yo has an impressive placed record in this division — six places from eight runs at 14-16f on good ground including a win — but a 37-day absence and the lowest OR in the field (55) cap expectations; Nicola Currie rides a horse that is most effective when settled at the rear and unleashed late, yet that is exactly the crowded space all five runners will be fighting over.

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying a hold-up style and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 2m Good To Firm contest at Newmarket's July course is almost certain to be run at a crawl in the early stages, with the field bunching together before someone is forced wide or makes an uncharacteristic forward move in the home straight. Vilaine Verlaine and Now The Eagle are the only two genuine hold-up horses occupying their natural rear positions, while Prince Quattro, Betelgeuse, and Dereham are all true hold-up types redistributed into midfield slots because the map cannot place all five at the rear. The race shape that emerges will almost certainly be a slow-burn, tactical affair that collapses into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs, with jockey quality and positional luck in the straight becoming the decisive factors. In a race this compressed and this tactical, horses who can quicken efficiently off a slow gallop — and who are settled enough to produce a genuine late burst — will hold the edge; this shape strongly favours runners with proven finishing speed over staying distance on fast ground rather than raw stamina grinders.

scenarios.title: Slow Burn Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls through the early stages and the race turns into a dash from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If the field crawls through the early stages and the race turns into a dash from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.title: One Horse Moves Early
scenarios.trigger: If one runner breaks from the pack in the back straight to force an uncharacteristic lead, changing the entire pace dynamic.
scenarios.body: If one runner breaks from the pack in the back straight to force an uncharacteristic lead, changing the entire pace dynamic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Outpace Field Late

watchPoints.text: Watch the early gallop — with five hold-up horses and no pace-setter, Now The Eagle or Vilaine Verlaine may be shuffled wide into the home straight if the field dawdles and then suddenly bunches, costing vital lengths at a critical moment.

Betelgeuse's 8-day turnaround is the shortest freshen-up in the field; if the horse shows any signs of fatigue or reluctance to load, discount it sharply despite Billy Loughnane's ability to manage it tactically.
Prince Quattro's 92-day absence is the longest layoff here and James Owen's 14-day form (7/40) is heavy volume but not high quality — fitness on return is a legitimate concern over 2m on fast ground.

Dereham's age (10) and lowest weight (122lbs) combination is worth monitoring — if Nicola Currie can secure an uncontested position just off a slow pace, the veteran's course-and-distance placed record makes it a natural each-way consideration in the sprint finish scenario.

The Good To Firm going is confirmed across all eight races on the card — any runner whose historical form is weighted towards soft or standard artificial surfaces (Now The Eagle at Stratford, Prince Quattro on AW) should be assessed carefully against this faster surface before accepting the form lines at face value.

races.name: Turners Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Seventy
runners_data.note: In-form front-runner with back-to-back wins recently (133121 form), Ross Burdon's yard in solid 14-day strike-rate at 2/3, 11 days since last run is ideal freshness, and Good to Firm going suits with 7/14 on similar going including two wins — the concern is being outpaced if the field quickens sharply despite her front-running role being perfectly suited here.

runners_data.name: Market House
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent type wearing tongue-tie/hood (tp/hg) who has form over extreme stamina trips including wins at 16f and 20f, making this 1m4f trip potentially on the sharp side; Mason Paetel's 3lb claim helps the handicap, but 43 days off (26-day jockey change flag) and a trainer strike-rate of just 6/53 over 14 days suggests limited confidence from connections.

runners_data.name: Green Team
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who will race at the rear — his recent form is all on Standard/artificial going (Southwell/Wolverhampton) and this Good to Firm turf at Newmarket is an unexplored surface for him in his last five runs, making the going angle a genuine query; the 7lb claim for Kyle McHugh partially offsets that concern, and at OR 65 he has slipped to a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Nuptown Girl
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who will want everything to happen late, but her recent Good to Firm record shows 0 wins and 0 places from two attempts (2/14 on sim-going), which is a material concern on today's surface; Ian Williams's 1/24 14-day strike-rate is modest and at OR 58 she needs a lot to go right for her in a race that may not be truly run.

runners_data.name: Belle Amie
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer whose last two wins came at 12f on Good (July course) and Standard, and David Simcock's Newmarket form is always worth noting — however, she is a true rear-runner pushed to a mapped midfield position because so many runners share similar profiles, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she may not get the deep cover she needs to produce her best; 13 days since her last run is fine freshness.

races.paceDynamic: Seventy is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and, with no genuine rival to press for the lead, should dictate an uncontested gallop from the front over this 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. Market House is also a prominent type but with five rivals including the clear pace-setter, she is unlikely to land quite as close to the wire as her natural style demands, and Belle Amie — a genuine hold-up horse — has been mapped further forward than she will actually race because the field carries more rear-runners than the map can display at the back. With Seventy able to control tempo without pressure, the pace is likely to be honest but not suicidal, favouring a horse that can travel in behind and pick up through the straight rather than one that needs a truly run race to grind rivals down. This race shape most favours a prominent-to-midfield profile that can sit close enough to Seventy to pounce in the final two furlongs without being exposed to a solo breakaway if the leader goes clear unchallenged.

watchPoints.text: Watch Seventy in the opening furlong — if she bowls clear unchallenged and establishes a three-length-plus lead by the two-furlong marker, the hold-up horses will have too much ground to make up on Good to Firm ground.

Market House's tongue-tie and 43-day absence (with a jockey change flagged) make her unpredictable early — if she pushes up to contest the lead with Seventy the pace dynamic shifts entirely and scenario C becomes live.
Green Team's entire recent form history is on artificial surfaces, and if he fails to handle the Good to Firm turf at Newmarket his hold-up profile is rendered irrelevant regardless of race shape.

Belle Amie is a natural rear-runner mapped further forward than her true style — watch where Alexandra Egan actually settles her in the first half-mile, as a wide or detached position could cost her the ground she needs late.

The 8:45 evening slot at Newmarket July is the last race of the card — check for any significant going deterioration through the day given repeated reports of Good to Firm, as this affects the premium on hold-up stamina versus prominent speed.
